title: Exact, total and filtered small categories
subject: math.CT
abstract: For a non-empty connected small category we compare four properties: being filtered; exactness of colimits of abelian groups; Grothendieck's total asphericity, which says that colimits of simplicial sets over the category are homotopy colimits; and being quasi-filtered, which means that two arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square and that two parallel arrows are equalized by an integral combination of arrows whose coefficients sum to 1. Each implies the next. We give a category of finite ordered hypergraphs that is totally aspherical and whose colimits are exact over no non-zero ring, and we show that the category of finite ordered two-graphs (sets of triples that meet every four-element set in an even number of triples) is quasi-filtered and not totally aspherical. With the example of Isbell and Mitchell, the three implications are strict. A conjecture in Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is therefore false; it holds for sifted categories, those over which colimits of sets commute with finite products.
comments:
This paper compares four properties of a non-empty connected small category: filtered, exact (colimits of abelian groups are exact), total in Grothendieck's sense (colimits of simplicial sets are homotopy colimits), and quasi-filtered. Each implies the next. Theorem A: a category of finite ordered hypergraphs (2|U| - 3e(U) > 0, closed embeddings) is total, and its colimits are exact over no non-zero ring. Theorem B: the category of finite ordered two-graphs is quasi-filtered and not total (its classifying space is simply connected with non-zero second homology mod 2). With the example of Isbell and Mitchell (1973) all three implications are strict. So the conjecture of Les Dérivateurs, Chapter II, manuscript p. 36ter, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is false; it holds for sifted categories (a category is filtered if and only if it is total and sifted).

Checks: the proofs taken from GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) runs were followed in full by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort high and at effort max (13 and 17 November 2026); Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max wrote the text and re-derived every proof; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked the finished text independently (25 November 2026): every statement and proof correct, Theorem B's non-totality proved again by another route, eight repairs of wording and citation, none changing a statement. Literature searched (arXiv, the web, the Hexagon catalogue): no statement of Theorems A or B found. No human has checked it; nothing is formalized. Text: AI-authored; none of it was written by a human. The submitter takes responsibility for the veracity of the text.

How it was produced. The mathematics comes from four research runs of GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, in November 2026, on the passage of Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs that asks whether totally aspherical categories are filtered: TOTAL_ASPHERICITY (the characterization of total categories by their categories of elements; exact implies total), PRESHEAF_TOTALITY (filtered if and only if total and sifted), TOTAL_EXACT_2 (the hypergraph category and Theorem A) and DER_FOLLOWUP (the two-graph category and Theorem B). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote this text on 25 November 2026: it reorganized the runs' proofs (one reduction, Proposition 3.2; the bridge split into Lemma 3.3 and its two uses) and gave its own arguments for Propositions 2.7, 2.8, the reduction in Proposition 5.7 with Lemmas 5.5, 5.6, and Lemmas 5.8, 5.9.

How it was checked. The proofs of TOTAL_EXACT_2 used here were followed in full by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort high and by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max (13 November 2026), and those of DER_FOLLOWUP by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max (17 November 2026); Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max reviewed PRESHEAF_TOTALITY (13 November 2026). A program independent of the runs searched the hypergraph category up to seven vertices for affine equalizers and found none, as Theorem A predicts. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, in a separate run, checked the finished text independently on 25 November 2026: before reading the proofs it attempted Theorem A itself (its attempt stopped at the step that Proposition 3.2 settles) and proved the non-totality in Theorem B by another route; it then followed every proof, opened Isbell-Mitchell 1973 and 1976, Adámek-Koubek-Reiterman 1981, Rosický (arXiv v2) and the edition of Les Dérivateurs at the statements used, compared the two French quotations with the edition, and searched the literature; it found every statement and proof correct and proposed eight repairs of wording and citation, none changing a statement, which the writer applied. The writer confirmed Adámek-Rosický (Definition 1.1, Theorem 1.6), Weibel's K-book (Chapter IV) and Jardine's lecture notes in free copies; Quillen 1973, Mac Lane, Weibel's homological algebra, Bousfield-Kan, Goerss-Jardine and Seidel are cited at the level a public table of contents confirms, or without a locator. Before posting, the main session, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, read every page, checked the edition's footnotes on Proposition 2.19 and the journal data of the references, and added the corrigendum of Rosický's paper. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized.
